clue.text: Father admitting look, ing grim

parts.note: FR is the standard abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
admitting something is owning up to it

explanation.surface: A father confesses something while looking stern.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'look, ing' is a scanning slip for 'looking'. 'admitting' looks like a container signal but here it simply means owning (up).
explanation.definitionFit: To frown is to wear a stern, scowling expression, so frowning describes a grim face.

clue.text: The first of several parking in turn

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word several is taken on its own

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
taken as written

explanation.surface: Several cars park one after another in sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in turn' reads as a phrase meaning 'one after another', but 'in' supplies letters and 'turn' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin is a rotation, which is what a turn can be.

clue.text: The businessman who takes too much interest

definitions.text: The businessman who takes too much interest

parts.words: The businessman who takes too much interest
parts.note: suggests a nosy person, but interest here is the charge on a loan, and taking too much of it is the mark of an extortionate moneylender

explanation.walkthrough: 'interest' pretends to mean curiosity; it is money charged on a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: A lender charging excessive rates on loans is the classic meaning of the word.

clue.text: A noble woman about fifty, quite incomparable

indicators.note: the noble woman goes around the fifty, enclosing it

parts.note: a woman holding a peerage, such as a countess, is a peeress
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A titled lady of about fifty is beyond compare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about fifty' reads as her age; 'about' actually puts PEERESS around L.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without equal has no peer to match it, so it is beyond comparison.

clue.text: Most powerful top men —-into mergers

indicators.note: the words top men and into are merged together and blended into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Bosses of mighty firms are drawn into corporate mergers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mergers' is the anagram signal working on TOP MEN plus INTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Being all-powerful, with unlimited authority, is the sense of the word.

clue.text: Attachment for a girl over the water

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above, or over, the second

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
the Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England

explanation.surface: Someone becomes fond of a girl living across the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attachment' suggests affection; it is an added building. The EXE is a river in Devon, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: An extension or outbuilding added on to a main building is attached to it.

clue.text: Offer pals poor exchange

indicators.note: the letters of pals poor are swapped around into a new order

explanation.surface: Friends who are short of money swap things.
explanation.definitionFit: A suggestion put forward for acceptance, such as a bid, is an offer.

clue.text: The French store getting censured

parts.note: la is a French word for the
a shed is a hut used for storing things

explanation.surface: A French storehouse comes in for criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: Being lashed by someone's tongue means being severely criticised.

clue.text: In winter miners need coats of fur

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters across winter miners

explanation.surface: In cold weather, men working underground need fur coats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'need' is a link word. The fur from the stoat's white winter coat is used for robes and trimmings.
explanation.definitionFit: The white winter pelt of the stoat is a prized fur used for ceremonial robes.

clue.text: Man given ring back unworn

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O

indicators.note: the word for unworn is turned around and read backwards

parts.note: unworn clothes are new

explanation.surface: A man receives a ring that comes back unworn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a general noun but is the definition for a first name; 'back' is the reversal signal on the word for unworn.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name, common in Wales, serves for any male.

clue.text: Engineers forced to be reasonable

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
a forced smile is a strained one

explanation.surface: Engineers are compelled to behave sensibly.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing moderation and self-control is being sensible and measured.

clue.text: Seethe when about two thousand is returned

indicators.note: the whole string built from about, two thousand and is is read backwards

parts.note: re means concerning, about
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two of them make MM

explanation.surface: Someone fumes when about two thousand pounds comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns the whole run REMMIS back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: To bubble gently below boiling, or to be quietly angry, is to seethe.

clue.text: Discretion in using fashion budget

parts.note: a mode is a style or fashion
a ration is an allowance, a budgeted amount

explanation.surface: Show restraint when spending your clothes allowance.
explanation.definitionFit: Avoiding excess and keeping within limits shows prudent restraint.

clue.text: Ugly things have a point certainly-or points

parts.note: E, east, is a point of the compass
yes is an emphatic agreement, like certainly
taken as written
E and S, east and south, are compass points

explanation.surface: Unsightly things certainly make a point, or several.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' means compass points: E and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsightly buildings or objects that offend the view are ugly things.

clue.text: An innovative device that may well be tagged

indicators.note: suggests the letters of tagged could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A new invention might well carry a label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may well be' signals that the letters of TAGGED can become the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A clever new contraption or gizmo is a gadget.

clue.text: Appearance in public is all-important to a photographer

explanation.surface: Being seen is vital to any photographer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both being seen in the media and the amount of light let onto film.

clue.text: The appearance of a page in school

indicators.note: the page goes inside the word for school

parts.note: a school of thought is a sect

explanation.surface: How a page looks in a school book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' means a group of followers, a SECT.
explanation.definitionFit: The look or outward appearance of something is its aspect.

clue.text: Sturdy but stupid lot

parts.note: thick is informal for stupid
a set is a group, a lot

explanation.surface: A strong but dim group of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavily built, stocky body is sturdy.

clue.text: A green compound for making incense

indicators.note: a compound is a mixture, so the letters of a green are mixed up

explanation.surface: A green chemical compound is used to make incense sticks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incense' looks like the noun for joss sticks; it is the verb meaning to anger.
explanation.definitionFit: To incense someone is to make them furious.

clue.text: A reptile keeping quiet concealed in the ground

indicators.note: the quiet letter is hidden away inside the word for ground

parts.note: terrain is ground or land
P, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A reptile keeps still, hiding in the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: P is piano, the music marking for 'quietly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater turtle is a kind of reptile.

clue.text: Summons the first lady's about to endorse

indicators.note: the first lady's name goes around the word for endorse

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis, giving Eve's
to OK something is to approve it

explanation.surface: A president's wife issues summonses she is about to back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the first lady' is not a president's wife but Eve, the first woman in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: To call up a memory or feeling is to summon it.

clue.text: Stirring up dirt is rotten

indicators.note: stirring mixes the letters of up dirt into a new order

explanation.surface: Stirring up dirt is a rotten thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stirring up' reads as one phrase, but 'up' is fodder alongside DIRT.
explanation.definitionFit: Decayed, foul-smelling matter is rotten.

clue.text: A vegetable too apt to be wrongly treated

indicators.note: the letters of too apt are handled wrongly and so come out rearranged

explanation.surface: A vegetable is all too likely to be mistreated.
explanation.definitionFit: The spud is a common starchy tuber, a vegetable.

clue.text: A fighter can't accept being checked out

indicators.note: the word can't takes in another piece, holding it inside

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, giving CANT
something being checked is on test

explanation.surface: A boxer refuses to be examined.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'can't' is ignored, and 'accept' means the shortened form takes the checking phrase inside it, splitting after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone competing in a bout or contest is a fighter in it.

clue.text: Mere colouring matter

explanation.surface: Just a bit of pigment.
explanation.definitionFit: A mere is a poetic word for a pool of water; a lake is also a crimson pigment.

clue.text: Advance due to the demise of the Left?

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
a demise is a death, an end

explanation.surface: Is a political advance due to the collapse of the Left?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advance' sounds like progress; it means to loan money.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance someone money is to loan it.

clue.text: Painter taking note Parisian Black is required

parts.note: re is a note of the sol-fa scale
noir is the French word for black

explanation.surface: An artist needs a note and some black paint from Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre-Auguste was a French Impressionist painter.

clue.text: Prolonged extra over

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Prolonged extra over' (8): 'Prolonged' defines EXTENDED, but 'extra over' gives no wordplay for it; the clue looks garbled and no search found the printed text.
